This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 01.09.2021 at about 07.30 a.m, the petitioner was proceeding with his Jupiter Scooter bearing No.KA-50-EA-9484 came from Doddaballapura Bengaluru Main Road, near Bakery, Rajanakunte, at that time suddenly the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-01-MA-4156 came with excessive speed, in rash and negligent manner, who was going in front of the Jupiter Scooter, without giving any signals, took sudden right turn and dashed against the Scooter.

Due to this the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 Navachethana hospital, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, wherein after first aid he was shifted to ESI hospital, Rajajinagar, wherein as per the advice of the doctor, he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/-
towards medical and other expenses and prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged 32 years and was working as Security and earning more than Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries, he is getting often and often severe headache and giddiness and unable to attend to his work from the date of accident,
due to which he sustained loss of income and undergone mental agony and sufferings.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending car driver and in this regard the Rajanakunite Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending Car.

Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 being the R.C.
Owner and the driver of said offending Car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Car, age, occupation,
income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and not due to negligent driving of the offending car and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 01.09.2021 at about 07.30 a.m, near Bakery, Rajanakunte Main Road, Yelahanka Taluk, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Car bearing registration No.KA-01-MA-4156 by its driver as allegedin the petition?

The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined five witnesses as PW.2 to 6 and through them got marked 32 documents as Ex.P.1 to 32 (Ex.P.15 marked twice) and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The respondent No.1 got examined as RW.1 and no documents has been marked and closed his side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and respondents and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 petition averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the counsel for respondents he admits that the accident road has got divider and it is two way road and that one car had caused accident to him and said car which has caused accident to him was coming from Bengaluru side and taking "U" turn and denied to the suggestion that he after overtaking the parked car hit against the car which was taking "U" turn and also denied to the suggestion that this accident occurred due to his negligence and not due to negligence of car driver and also denied to the suggestion that he overtook another parked car and hit against the car which was taking "U" turn and hence this accident occurred and also stated that since he was taking treatment at hospital, complaint was lodged little later.
10.

Further, PW.2 is MRI at M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru and he has produced MLC extract,
Police intimation, Inpatient record and Outpatient record of the petitioner as per Ex.P.16 to 19.
11.

Further, PW.3 is MRI at Navachethana hospital, Bengaluru and he has produced MLC register,
Police intimation and Inpatient record of the petitioner as per Ex.P.21 to 23.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondents counsel he (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 admits that still Dr.Krishna Prasad is working in their hospital and he do not know the contents of documents produced by him.

sentences.text: Further, PW.4 is a Doctor and he has produced Case sheet of the petitioner as per Ex.P.25.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondents counsel he admits that as per Ex.P.25 the petitioner came only for observation and he has not treated the petitioner, one Dr.Chandrakanth and Dr.Mandeep have treated the petitioner and said doctors are still working in their hospital.
13.

Further, PW.5 is MRI at M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru and he has produced MLC register,
Police intimation, Inpatient record and X-rays of the petitioner as per Ex.P.27 to 30.
During the course of cross-examination by the respondents counsel he stated that he do not know who had treated the petitioner.

14. Further, PW.6 is a doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated in his chief-examination evidence that the petitioner has sustained D4, D6, D7 anterior wedge compression fracture, left hemothorax, multiple facial bone fracture and bilateral humerus fracture and he assessed whole body physical disability at 36% (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 and also stated that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/- and he has produced Clinical notes and X-ray of the petitioner as per Ex.P.31 and 32.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondents counsel he admits that he has not personally treated the petitioner and he has assessed disability after verifying Discharge summary and Wound certificate and has not seen IP records and also admits that as per the recent X-ray fractures are united and implants are in-situ and that to improve the range of movements physiotherapy treatment is advised and as per the Discharge summary physiotherapy treatment was advised and he has not seen the follow-up records regarding taking physiotherapy treatment and he has not assessed functional disability and has not given estimation regarding future medical expenses and denied to the suggestion that since he was not treated doctor,
he has not competent person to assess disability.
15.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 32 documents as Ex.P.1 to 32 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Rajanakunte Police against the driver of the offending Car.

Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against driver of the (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 offending Car for his rash and negligent driving of Car who caused the accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.3 is copy of IMV report which discloses involvement of both vehicles in the alleged accident and both vehicles are damaged.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner/ respondent No.2 of the offending Car.

Ex.P.5 is copy of Reply to notice wherein the owner-cum-driver of the offending Car has stated that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and he had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident and said offending car had insurance policy as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Wound certificate which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Car and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Car and caused grievous injuries to the petitioner and also stated that the offending vehicle had no insurance policy as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.8 to 10 are the Discharge summaries which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in Navachethana hospital from 01.09.2021 to 02.09.2021 for 02 days and again (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 admitted as inpatient in M.S.Ramaiah hospital from 02.09.2021 to 21.09.2021 for 20 days and again admitted Mohan .K.S vs Friends Motor Driving School on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184368036/
4 as inpatient in Prasad hospital from 29.09.2021 to 05.10.2021 for 07 days due to accidental injuries.

16. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, which clearly establishes that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 01.09.2021 at about 07.30 a.m, on Doddaballapura Bengaluru Main Road,
near Bakery, Rajanakunte, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing No.KA-01-MA-4156, by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to the accident he was (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 hale and healthy and was aged 32 years and was working as Security and earning more than Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses and.
Due to accidental injuries, he sustained pain and sufferings, loss of income and became permanent disabled.
18. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.

However, he has produced Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.12 Driving licence of the petitioner,
wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 15.03.1983 and the alleged accident occurred on 01.09.2021.
Hence, eventhough these documents are taken into consideration in the absence of any other evidence, it appears that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 38 years.

Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 38 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 is 15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.
20.

According to the evidence of PW.6, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained D4, D6, D7 anterior wedge compression fracture, left hemothorax, multiple facial bone fracture and bilateral humerus fracture and he assessed whole body physical disability at 36%.

Hence, considering the evidence of PW.6 and nature of injuries sustained and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional Mohan .K.S vs Friends Motor Driving School on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184368036/
5 disability of the petitioner at 15%.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries as per Ex.P.8 to 10, (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 according to which he was admitted in Navachethana hospital, M.S.Ramaiah hospital and Prasad hospital, as inpatient for 29 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.
22. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.6 doctor and Ex.P.14, 30, 32 X-rays, Ex.P.18, 23 and 29 Inpatient records, Ex.P.19 Outpatient record, Ex.P.25 Case sheet and Ex.P.31 Clinical notes and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.
23. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for nearly 29 days as inpatient as per Ex.P.8 (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 to 10.

Considering the nature of injuries,
treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast four months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.60,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 4) under this head.
24. Medical expenses:-

As per Ex.P.13 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses i.e., inpatient bill for Rs.18,275/- and as admitted by the PW.1 in the cross-examination that his Medical bills was paid by the ESI and he volunteers that some bills were paid by ESI and hence whatever bills reimbursed by the ESI has not been produced before the tribunal and has denied to the suggestion that Ex.P.13 was reimbursed by ESI.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.18,275/- under this head.

25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
(SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 26.
Future medical expenses:-
According to doctor PW.6 the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.

Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case,
under this head the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 4,05,000-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 40,000-00

3 . Attendant charges, extra 40,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  4. Medical Expenses 18,275-00  5. Loss of future amenities and 40,000-00  unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid up 60,000-00  period  7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 6,33,275-00 28.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,33,275/- with (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
29. Regarding liability:- As per Ex.P.7 Charge sheet the offending vehicle had no insurance policy as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending car.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, he got himself examined as RW.1.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that he is the owner of the offending car and also admits that Police have seized the offending car after the accident and he also given reply to the notice and he went to Police Station and get released the offending car by executing indemnity bond and he has not challenged the Charge sheet and also stated that as on the date of accident the offending car had no insurance policy and also admits that the criminal case with respect to accident is pending before the criminal court.
30.

Therefore, on going through the oral and documentary evidence of the petitioner and respondents, respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and respondent No.2 being the driver are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondents are liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.6,33,275/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
31. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,33,275/- (Rupees Six lakhs thirty three thousand two hundred and seventy five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.1238/2022 deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
